items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A loading puzzle opens the lesson: lift a 100 kg box straight onto a truck, or push it up a 4 m plank?

The ramp introduces **load**, **effort** and **mechanical advantage**, and a work argument gives **MA = L ÷ h**. A crowbar names the parts of a **lever**, a coin balance gives the **law of the lever**, and three tools are sorted into the **three classes**.

A well bucket introduces the **fixed pulley**, and a **movable pulley** halves the effort.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• work done, W = F × s, and the joule

• weight of an object, mg

• gravitational potential energy, U = mgh

• work–energy theorem: work done = change in energy

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Define mechanical advantage.

**2.** State and apply the law of the lever and identify the classes of levers with examples.

**3.** Calculate the mechanical advantage of an inclined plane and pulleys.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• Left: a man lifts a **100 kg** box straight up onto a truck floor **1 m** high.

• Right: he pushes the same box up a **4 m** plank.

**Answer to Question 1**

Most students pick the **plank**: it feels easier because it needs **less force**.

**Answer to Question 2**

At least its weight: 100 × 10 = **1000 N**.

**Answer to Question 3**

Take a vote. **Do not reveal the answer yet.** Question 8 and Practice 1 settle it.

**What this shows**

(a) A box of mass m **lifted straight up** through a height h. The man's push on the box acts up; the box's weight, mg, acts down.

**Answer to Question 4**

They are **equal**: effort = load = **mg**.

Question 4. Answer is on pointer 2.

chunks.name: Lifting or pushing up a ramp

items.text:
**What this shows**

(b) The same box **pushed slowly up a smooth ramp** of length L to the same height h, with a force F′ along the ramp.

**Answer to Question 5**

**W = F′ × L.**

**Answer to Question 6**

**U = mgh.** By the work–energy theorem, **F′ × L = mgh**.

**Answer to Question 7**

**mg ÷ F′ = L ÷ h.**

script.x: Show (a) again, then reveal (b). Pointer 1 sets (b) up. Build the result on the board.
Questions 5 to 7 in order. Answers are on pointers 2 to 4.

items.text:
**Answer to Question 8**

**No.** Ignoring friction, the work done is **mgh either way**. The ramp needs a **smaller force**, but over a **longer distance**.

script.x: Show the key idea: mechanical advantage.
Question 8 settles the hook. Answer is on pointer 1.
Show the conclusion box.

items.prompt: A machine lifts a 900 N load when an effort of 300 N is applied. Its mechanical advantage is
Two smooth ramps lead up to the same platform. Ramp P is 3 m long and ramp Q is 6 m long. To push the same box up, ramp Q needs
options: half the effort and half the work
half the effort and the same work
the same effort and the same work
twice the effort and half the work

items.prompt: Fill in the blanks: a smooth ramp 2.5 m long leads up a step 50 cm high. Its mechanical advantage is ____, and the effort needed to push a 400 N trolley up it is ____ N.

items.text:
**On Question 2**

**B**: MA = L ÷ h **doubles**, so the effort **halves**; the work done, mgh, is **the same**.

**On Question 3**

**A**: 50 cm = 0.5 m, so MA = 2.5 ÷ 0.5 = **5**, and effort = 400 ÷ 5 = **80 N**. (B) forgets to convert cm.

script.x: Activate each question and explain depending on time available.
Pointers 1, 2 and 3 carry the reasoning.

items.text:
**What this shows**

A crowbar resting on a small stone, used to lift a heavy rock. The effort pushes the long end down.

**Answer to Question 9**

The **effort end**, the long end, farther from the small stone it turns about.

**Answer to Question 10**

So that the effort is **much farther** from the stone than the load is.

script.x: Questions 9 and 10 with the unlabelled crowbar. Answers are on pointers 2 and 3.
Then show the key idea and the labelled crowbar: the stone is the fulcrum, and the two distances are the load arm and the effort arm.
Restate the answers in the new words: the effort end moves farther because the effort arm is longer; the stone goes near the rock to make the load arm short.

items.text:
**What this shows**

A scale hung from a string at its middle (the fulcrum), with cups of coins on either side. In each row of the table, the scale stays **level**.

**Answer to Question 11**

They are **equal** in every row: **20 and 20** in the first three rows, **30 and 30** in the last.

**Answer to Question 12**

It is **halved**: 2 coins at 10 cm, 4 coins at 5 cm.

script.x: Show the scale and the table. Pointer 1 sets them up. Draw the table on the board and fill in the last two columns with the students.
Questions 11 and 12. Answers are on pointers 2 and 3.
Show the key idea.

items.text:
**Answer to Question 13**

**Class I**: the fulcrum. **Class II**: the load. **Class III**: the effort.

script.x: Show the three ways of arranging the fulcrum, load and effort.
Question 13. Answer is on pointer 1.

items.text:
**What this shows**

Three tools at work: **scissors** cutting paper, a **wheelbarrow** carrying bricks, and **tweezers** picking up a bead.

**Answer to Question 14**

**Scissors**: the screw is the fulcrum, between the handles (effort) and the paper (load): **class I**.

**Wheelbarrow**: the axle is the fulcrum, the bricks (load) in the middle, the effort at the handles: **class II**.

**Tweezers**: the joined end is the fulcrum, the fingers press in the middle (effort), the bead at the tips (load): **class III**.

**Answer to Question 15**

**Less than 1**: the effort is more than the load. But the tips move more than the fingers, so we can hold small things **gently and precisely**.

script.x: Show the three tools. Pointer 1 sets them up.
Questions 14 and 15. Answers are on pointers 2 and 3.
Show the conclusion box, pointing back to the three arrangements.

items.prompt: Identify the class of each lever: (i) nutcracker, (ii) pliers, (iii) fishing rod.
A crowbar is used to lift a stone weighing 1200 N. The load arm is 0.3 m and the effort arm is 1.2 m. The effort needed and the mechanical advantage are

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**A**: nutcracker, load in the middle: **class II**; pliers, fulcrum in the middle: **class I**; fishing rod, effort in the middle: **class III**.

items.text:
**What this shows**

A woman draws a bucket of water from a well. The rope runs over a wheel fixed to the frame above the well.

**Answer to Question 16**

She pulls **down**; the bucket moves **up**.

**Answer to Question 17**

**100 N.** The same rope pulls up on the bucket with the force she applies.

**Answer to Question 18**

**Pulling down is easier** than lifting up: she can use her own weight, and she does not have to lean over the well.

script.x: Show the well. Pointer 1 sets it up.
Questions 16 to 18 in order. Answers are on pointers 2 to 4.
Show the key idea.

items.text:
**What this shows**

(a) A **fixed pulley**. (b) A **movable pulley**: the load hangs from the pulley itself. (c) A movable pulley used with a fixed pulley.

**Answer to Question 19**

**Two.**

**Answer to Question 20**

2E = 100 N, so **E = 50 N**. MA = 100 ÷ 50 = **2**.

**Answer to Question 21**

**2 m.** Half the force, twice the distance: the **work done is the same**.

script.x: Show the three pulleys. Pointer 1 sets them up.
Question 19. Answer is on pointer 2.
Then reveal the labelled movable pulley on the right: E on each segment, so 2E holds up the pulley and the load of 100 N.
Questions 20 and 21. Answers are on pointers 3 and 4.
Show the conclusion box, pointing back to the three pulleys.

items.prompt: To raise a 600 N load with a single movable pulley, the effort needed is
The load on a movable pulley rises by 3 m. The length of rope the person pulls is

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**C**: two rope segments hold up the load, so effort = 600 ÷ 2 = **300 N**.

**On Question 2**

**C**: **6 m**. Both segments must become 3 m shorter.
